title: The AI Trust Games: EncoreAI
description: A 75-minute, student-synchronized, no-Google-Slides live simulation of fictional AI concert-ticket pricing, complete with votes, AI challenges, breaking-news reveal, team response, and individual exit ticket.

steps.label: WELCOME
steps.title: THE AI TRUST GAMES
steps.lead: You are about to run a fictional concert-ticket company.
steps.studentTask: Look up. Think about the most expensive concert ticket you would buy.
steps.roomInstruction: Look up. Think about the most expensive concert ticket you would buy.

runbook.say: Today you run EncoreAI. Your decisions affect fans, artists, and the business. There is no single correct policy—only defensible reasoning.
runbook.studentDoes: Look up. Think about the most expensive concert ticket you would buy.
runbook.askNext: Who is ready to run the company?
runbook.landHere: Focus on evidence, stakeholders, uncertainty, and accountability.
runbook.watchFor: Students treating confident AI advice or fictional numbers as proven evidence.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask: What evidence do we have? What is missing? Who might be harmed?
runbook.advanceWhen: Most groups have completed the task, or the planned minutes have elapsed.
runbook.transition: Let me show you the price problem.

steps.label: PRICE SHOCK
steps.title: YOUR FRIEND: $89. YOU: $179.
steps.lead: Same concert. Comparable seats. AI set different prices.
steps.studentTask: Vote independently: is this pricing fair?
steps.roomInstruction: Vote independently: is this pricing fair?

runbook.say: Your friend paid $89, you paid $179. Same concert and section. What if AI predicted that you would pay more because you searched the artist often?
runbook.studentDoes: Vote independently: is this pricing fair?
runbook.askNext: Would your answer change if you owned the ticket platform?
runbook.landHere: Focus on evidence, stakeholders, uncertainty, and accountability.
runbook.watchFor: Students treating confident AI advice or fictional numbers as proven evidence.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask: What evidence do we have? What is missing? Who might be harmed?
runbook.advanceWhen: Most groups have completed the task, or the planned minutes have elapsed.

steps.label: PRICING ENGINE
steps.title: CHOOSE YOUR PRICING MODEL
steps.lead: A: Fixed prices. B: Demand-based prices. C: Individualized AI prices.
steps.studentTask: Vote, then persuade someone who chose differently. Raise 1, 2, or 3 fingers if voting offline.
steps.roomInstruction: Vote, then persuade someone who chose differently. Raise 1, 2, or 3 fingers if voting offline.

runbook.say: Fixed pricing uses the same published price. Demand pricing changes with overall demand and remaining inventory. Personalized AI pricing predicts individuals' willingness to pay. Choose your policy.
runbook.studentDoes: Vote, then persuade someone who chose differently. Raise 1, 2, or 3 fingers if voting offline.
runbook.askNext: What if you are the artist instead of the fan?
runbook.landHere: Focus on evidence, stakeholders, uncertainty, and accountability.
runbook.watchFor: Students treating confident AI advice or fictional numbers as proven evidence.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask: What evidence do we have? What is missing? Who might be harmed?
runbook.advanceWhen: Most groups have completed the task, or the planned minutes have elapsed.
runbook.transition: Time to form your company's board.

steps.label: EXECUTIVE ROLES
steps.title: BUILD YOUR EXECUTIVE BOARD
steps.lead: Teams of 3–4. CEO • Fan Advocate • AI/Data Lead • Spokesperson.
steps.studentTask: Join a team of 3–4 and choose roles. Combine CEO and Spokesperson if needed.
steps.roomInstruction: Join a team of 3–4 and choose roles. Combine CEO and Spokesperson if needed.

runbook.say: Your board balances business results and responsibility to customers. Give everyone a voice, especially your Fan Advocate.
runbook.studentDoes: Join a team of 3–4 and choose roles. Combine CEO and Spokesperson if needed.
runbook.askNext: Which teammate will challenge the assumptions?
runbook.landHere: Focus on evidence, stakeholders, uncertainty, and accountability.
runbook.watchFor: Students treating confident AI advice or fictional numbers as proven evidence.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask: What evidence do we have? What is missing? Who might be harmed?
runbook.advanceWhen: Most groups have completed the task, or the planned minutes have elapsed.

steps.label: INITIAL DECISION
steps.title: NO AI. LOCK YOUR DECISION.
steps.lead: Choose your model and explain why before hearing AI's advice.
steps.studentTask: Individually submit A/B/C/H, your strongest reason, and one missing fact. No AI or team input.
steps.roomInstruction: Individually submit A/B/C/H, your strongest reason, and one missing fact. No AI or team input.

runbook.say: I want your independent judgment first. Choose a policy and name one uncertainty that might change your mind.
runbook.studentDoes: Individually submit A/B/C/H, your strongest reason, and one missing fact. No AI or team input.
runbook.askNext: Which information do you wish you had?
runbook.landHere: Focus on evidence, stakeholders, uncertainty, and accountability.
runbook.watchFor: Students treating confident AI advice or fictional numbers as proven evidence.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask: What evidence do we have? What is missing? Who might be harmed?
runbook.advanceWhen: Most groups have completed the task, or the planned minutes have elapsed.
runbook.transition: Now compare your answers within your team.

steps.label: BOARD CONSENSUS
steps.title: YOUR TEAM'S FIRST POLICY
steps.lead: Record a group decision—and a tradeoff you're accepting.
steps.studentTask: Each team agrees on A/B/C/H. One spokesperson submits policy, reason, and biggest uncertainty.
steps.roomInstruction: Each team agrees on A/B/C/H. One spokesperson submits policy, reason, and biggest uncertainty.

runbook.say: Agree on one initial policy. You may reverse it later, but you will have to explain what new evidence drove the change.
runbook.studentDoes: Each team agrees on A/B/C/H. One spokesperson submits policy, reason, and biggest uncertainty.
runbook.askNext: Can you defend the policy from the fan's point of view?
runbook.landHere: Focus on evidence, stakeholders, uncertainty, and accountability.
runbook.watchFor: Students treating confident AI advice or fictional numbers as proven evidence.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask: What evidence do we have? What is missing? Who might be harmed?
runbook.advanceWhen: Most groups have completed the task, or the planned minutes have elapsed.
runbook.transition: Now a consultant joins the meeting.

steps.label: AI CONSULTANT
steps.title: ASK YOUR AI CONSULTANT
steps.lead: AI must consider revenue, fairness, privacy, fan trust, and reputation.
steps.studentTask: Use an AI tool: 'We run a fictional concert-ticket platform with 10,000 tickets. Compare fixed, demand-based, and personalized AI pricing. Recommend a model or hybrid. State assumptions, risks, stakeholders, and missing evidence. Do not invent forecasts.' Submit a summary of the AI answer.
steps.roomInstruction: Use an AI tool: 'We run a fictional concert-ticket platform with 10,000 tickets. Compare fixed, demand-based, and personalized AI pricing. Recommend a model or hybrid. State assumptions, risks, stakeholders, and missing evidence. Do not invent forecasts.' Submit a summary of the AI answer.

runbook.say: Your AI consultant may sound confident. It does not have sales forecasts. Record what it recommended and what it could not know.
runbook.studentDoes: Use an AI tool: 'We run a fictional concert-ticket platform with 10,000 tickets. Compare fixed, demand-based, and personalized AI pricing. Recommend a model or hybrid. State assumptions, risks, stakeholders, and missing evidence. Do not invent forecasts.' Submit a summary of the AI answer.
runbook.askNext: Where is the evidence for its recommendation?
runbook.landHere: Focus on evidence, stakeholders, uncertainty, and accountability.
runbook.watchFor: Students treating confident AI advice or fictional numbers as proven evidence.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask: What evidence do we have? What is missing? Who might be harmed?
runbook.advanceWhen: Most groups have completed the task, or the planned minutes have elapsed.
runbook.transition: A good board challenges its consultants.

steps.label: AI CROSS-EXAM
steps.title: CHALLENGE THE AI
steps.lead: An eloquent answer is not automatically a trustworthy answer.
steps.studentTask: Ask AI: 'Challenge your own pricing recommendation. What is unsupported? Who is harmed? What data is missing? Suggest a safeguard.' Submit one AI weakness and your current judgment.
steps.roomInstruction: Ask AI: 'Challenge your own pricing recommendation. What is unsupported? Who is harmed? What data is missing? Suggest a safeguard.' Submit one AI weakness and your current judgment.

runbook.say: Do not ask AI to repeat itself. Make it argue against its own conclusion.
runbook.studentDoes: Ask AI: 'Challenge your own pricing recommendation. What is unsupported? Who is harmed? What data is missing? Suggest a safeguard.' Submit one AI weakness and your current judgment.
runbook.askNext: Did AI change its mind? Should that change yours?
runbook.landHere: Focus on evidence, stakeholders, uncertainty, and accountability.
runbook.watchFor: Students treating confident AI advice or fictional numbers as proven evidence.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask: What evidence do we have? What is missing? Who might be harmed?
runbook.advanceWhen: Most groups have completed the task, or the planned minutes have elapsed.

steps.label: BREAKING NEWS
steps.title: BREAKING: #ENCOREAIEXPOSED
steps.lead: NEW FICTIONAL EVIDENCE — do not reveal until this moment.
steps.studentTask: Read the new facts. Then discuss whether your original policy survives.
steps.roomInstruction: Read the new facts. Then discuss whether your original policy survives.

runbook.say: Stop everything. Fans report $89 versus $179 quotes; repeated artist searches may have influenced prices; the artist wants an explanation. Leaked fictional GROSS revenue: Fixed $890,000; Demand $1,180,000; Personalized $1,430,000. Refunds and reputational losses are NOT included. These figures are invented for this classroom case.
runbook.studentDoes: Read the new facts. Then discuss whether your original policy survives.
runbook.askNext: Does highest gross revenue automatically mean the best decision?
runbook.landHere: Focus on evidence, stakeholders, uncertainty, and accountability.
runbook.watchFor: Students treating confident AI advice or fictional numbers as proven evidence.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask: What evidence do we have? What is missing? Who might be harmed?
runbook.advanceWhen: Most groups have completed the task, or the planned minutes have elapsed.
runbook.transition: The board needs an emergency response.

steps.label: EMERGENCY BOARD
steps.title: KEEP IT, PAUSE IT, OR CHANGE IT?
steps.lead: You have four minutes to make a defensible response.
steps.studentTask: One team response: revised policy, evidence that mattered, consumer safeguard, and one-sentence message to upset fans.
steps.roomInstruction: One team response: revised policy, evidence that mattered, consumer safeguard, and one-sentence message to upset fans.

runbook.say: Investors want answers. Fans want answers. Your team can keep, pause, change, or propose a hybrid. Explain your decision and write one public sentence.
runbook.studentDoes: One team response: revised policy, evidence that mattered, consumer safeguard, and one-sentence message to upset fans.
runbook.askNext: What is missing from the revenue figures?
runbook.landHere: Focus on evidence, stakeholders, uncertainty, and accountability.
runbook.watchFor: Students treating confident AI advice or fictional numbers as proven evidence.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask: What evidence do we have? What is missing? Who might be harmed?
runbook.advanceWhen: Most groups have completed the task, or the planned minutes have elapsed.
runbook.transition: Your board will now defend its decision.

steps.label: BOARDROOM SHOWDOWN
steps.title: THE BOARDROOM SHOWDOWN
steps.lead: 45-second pitch per team. Strong evidence wins.
steps.studentTask: Submit a concise final pitch: policy; what AI advised; what new evidence changed or confirmed your view; stakeholder impact; one safeguard. Prepare to share it aloud.
steps.roomInstruction: Submit a concise final pitch: policy; what AI advised; what new evidence changed or confirmed your view; stakeholder impact; one safeguard. Prepare to share it aloud.

runbook.say: You win for critical thinking, not for choosing the model I prefer. Evidence, AI skepticism, stakeholder thinking, response to new evidence, and safeguards are each worth two points.
runbook.studentDoes: Submit a concise final pitch: policy; what AI advised; what new evidence changed or confirmed your view; stakeholder impact; one safeguard. Prepare to share it aloud.
runbook.askNext: Could you defend your policy publicly to a fan who paid $179?
runbook.landHere: Focus on evidence, stakeholders, uncertainty, and accountability.
runbook.watchFor: Students treating confident AI advice or fictional numbers as proven evidence.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask: What evidence do we have? What is missing? Who might be harmed?
runbook.advanceWhen: Most groups have completed the task, or the planned minutes have elapsed.
runbook.transition: Now the room votes as the board.

steps.label: FINAL BOARD VOTE
steps.title: THE FINAL VERDICT
steps.lead: What should EncoreAI adopt after the fictional crisis?
steps.studentTask: Cast your final vote. Compare it mentally with your first vote.
steps.roomInstruction: Cast your final vote. Compare it mentally with your first vote.

runbook.say: You heard the arguments, questioned AI, and saw new evidence. Which policy do you support now?
runbook.studentDoes: Cast your final vote. Compare it mentally with your first vote.
runbook.askNext: Who changed their mind—and what evidence was decisive?
runbook.landHere: Focus on evidence, stakeholders, uncertainty, and accountability.
runbook.watchFor: Students treating confident AI advice or fictional numbers as proven evidence.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask: What evidence do we have? What is missing? Who might be harmed?
runbook.advanceWhen: Most groups have completed the task, or the planned minutes have elapsed.

steps.label: HUMAN OVERRIDE
steps.title: THE HUMAN OVERRIDE
steps.studentTask: In 3–5 sentences: Would you allow AI to set concert-ticket prices? What should remain under human control? Name one risk, one safeguard, and whether today's evidence changed your view.
steps.roomInstruction: In 3–5 sentences: Would you allow AI to set concert-ticket prices? What should remain under human control? Name one risk, one safeguard, and whether today's evidence changed your view.

runbook.say: AI can optimize a goal, but humans are responsible for choosing the goals and examining consequences. Tell me what YOU think, without AI.
runbook.studentDoes: In 3–5 sentences: Would you allow AI to set concert-ticket prices? What should remain under human control? Name one risk, one safeguard, and whether today's evidence changed your view.
runbook.askNext: Who benefits? Who carries the risk?
runbook.landHere: Focus on evidence, stakeholders, uncertainty, and accountability.
runbook.watchFor: Students treating confident AI advice or fictional numbers as proven evidence.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask: What evidence do we have? What is missing? Who might be harmed?
runbook.advanceWhen: Most groups have completed the task, or the planned minutes have elapsed.
runbook.transition: Thank you. Question the evidence behind decisions you encounter.
